questions.question: Explain the difference between knowledge of results and knowledge of performance, using a sporting example.

points.text: Knowledge of results (KR) is feedback about the outcome of performance, while knowledge of performance (KP) is feedback about the quality of technique. Example: In golf, KR is knowing the ball landed in the bunker (the result), while KP is the coach telling the player their weight transfer was late and they came over the top of the ball (the technique). KR tells you what happened; KP tells you why

questions.question: Why is positive feedback particularly important for beginners?

points.text: Positive feedback is important for beginners because it builds their confidence and motivation, which are fragile in the early stages of learning. When beginners receive encouragement for what they do correctly, they are more likely to persist and continue practising. questions.question: Describe the difference between extrinsic and intrinsic feedback and explain when each is most effective.

points.text: Extrinsic feedback comes from outside the performer (coach, video, scoreboard), while intrinsic feedback comes from within the performer (kinaesthesia, proprioception, feel). Extrinsic feedback is most effective for beginners who lack the experience to self-assess, and during skill acquisition when the performer needs external information about their technique. questions.question: A basketball player misses a free throw. Give an example of negative feedback a coach could give. How does this differ from criticism?

points.text: Negative feedback: "Your elbow was flared out to the side - keep it tucked under the ball and aligned with the basket." This is constructive negative feedback because it identifies the specific error and provides a clear correction. Criticism would be "That was a terrible shot" - this tells the player nothing about what went wrong or how to improve.

questions.question: Explain why an elite performer relies more on intrinsic feedback than extrinsic feedback during competition.

questions.question: A coach tells a swimmer "your hand entry was too wide on that lap." Identify the type(s) of feedback being used and explain why it is appropriate for this performer.
